REVERSING the earlier proposal — it was wrong on the facts. 'Last logged 2026-02-24' is the date of your last Push A, not the last time you chose to do face pulls: only one Push A has run since, a 34-minute 21:58 session where the last THREE exercises collapsed together. Your actual record here is 22 of 24 sets across 12 sessions — 92%, better than most of your leg work. And this is the only external-rotation and only posterior-shoulder work in a 24-set day carrying 16 anterior sets. Put it back.

Face pulls are the only loaded lift in your plan with repMin = repMax (15-15), so the progression rule fires EVERY session and the load can only climb. It went 17.5 to 40 lb, where a rope face pull is a trap-driven high row, not a cuff movement — then sat stuck at 40 for six sessions. It is already back on that path: 20.5 to 25.5 in eight days. A 12-15 range lets it progress by control and reps instead of by the pin.

Every bit of core work you do is spinal flexion — 6 cable-crunch sets plus leg raises — against deadlifts topping 255x5 and rows at 150x8. Nothing resists rotation. Plank is also 3 of 10 sets across 5 sessions (30%), the second-deadest slot. Move it ahead of the Push A lateral raise so its one Push A exposure starts on fresh arms instead of the dregs.

Your legs were 100% bilateral — no single-leg work, so a stronger leg can hide a left/right gap that is judged on stage. A 4-seat trainer panel picked this over the Smith squat (bilateral, fixes nothing) and kettlebells (cap 30 lb, too light) as the one move that adds a squat pattern AND fixes symmetry. Start ~30/hand and light: the first sessions are to find balance and each leg's baseline. Weaker leg first, match — never beat — its reps. Off-ramp: if balance/knee/recovery suffers near prep, swap to single-leg leg press.
Keep quad volume about flat while the split squat is added: trim LegsA leg extension 3→2 sets (net +1 set on the day). Reverse anytime.

You did face pulls on Push A last night and wrote "Do you have a brain?" next to them, and tonight's Pull A asks for them again — this drops them from Pull A only, so they stay on your two push days, where nothing else trains the back of the shoulder, and come off a day that already runs six sets of pulldowns and rows.

On Pull B you skipped the face pulls yourself and wrote that running the same corrective on back-to-back days was insane — this makes the plan say what you already did, leaving Pull B's thirteen other back sets to cover the rear delt and keeping face pulls on the two push days.

Pull A gives your biceps six direct sets and your only horizontal row three, and on 24 July all three row sets went at 105 for ten, eleven and ten with nothing falling off — this makes it four sets so the rowing on your back day at least matches the curling.

Close-grip pulldown asks ten to twelve reps and you finished every 120 lb set at exactly ten on both of your last two Pull B nights — the weight only moves when every set reaches the top of the range, so this asks eight to ten and the tens you already do earn the next plate.

Legs A asks four sets of calf raises and you have done exactly two both times this block, 260 for fifteen and fifteen — and because the weight only rises when you complete every set the plan asks for, those two perfect sets currently count for nothing, so this makes the prescription the two sets you actually do.
Push B already has the reverse pec deck working the back of your shoulders, so face pulls are doing that job twice in one session — Push A has no reverse pec deck, so they stay on that day.

You asked whether three sets is right — both times you have done three on this day your third set came in at ten after two sets of twelve, so this makes it two if you would rather have the honest number.

You already approved moving this ahead of the Push A lateral raise on 23 July, but that card carried no position for the app to apply, so nothing moved and it still ran sixth on both Push A nights since — this is the same change with the number it was missing.

Dips are a pressing movement, but on Push B they run sixth, behind six straight sets of crossovers and rear-delt flies — this moves them up behind the chest press so both of your presses happen before the isolation work instead of after it.

Still open and unanswered, and it is on tonight's card: Push A's rope pushdown asks ten to twelve and your six sets there came in at eight, seven, nine and eight, seven, eight — not one set inside the range all block, so the weight can never move, and twelve to fifteen makes it a slot you can actually finish.

The program trainer wanted to hold this until two more Legs A nights are logged, which puts it in September — I am putting it in front of you now instead, because a question you cannot answer is worse than one you decline.

Face pulls have now come off all four of your days, so the back of your shoulder is down to five sets in the whole week and only two of them are on Push A — a night that carries thirteen sets of chest and front-shoulder work — and on 14 August you took both of those two at 90 for twelve without dropping a rep, so this makes Push A three sets, the same three you already do on Push B.

This is the other half of the card above, and they only work together: your last exercise has come in short on 3, 14 and 16 August, and on Push A the lift sitting last is the reverse pec deck, so adding a third set without moving it just puts more work in the spot that already gets eaten — this runs it fifth, straight after the shoulder press and ahead of the triceps and lateral raises, so your rear delts get a fresh slot instead of the dregs.

You accepted exactly this change on Legs B yesterday and Legs A still has the old ceiling on it — the hanging leg raise carries no weight, so reps are the only thing about it that can grow, and on both 26 July and 2 August your first two Legs A sets finished at twelve, which is the top of what that slot asks, so it is frozen there and can never ask for more; twelve to fifteen makes twelve the floor instead of the ceiling on both leg days.

Same change on the other leg day, and they belong together — the Legs B cable crunch sits at the same 60 and finished at twelve on 16 August, so leaving it at twelve to fifteen would freeze it on one day while the other one climbs.

Your last four Pull B nights ran the incline curl at 25 for ten, ten and then eight on 21 July and nine on 28 July, 15 August and 25 August — the first two sets hit the top of the range every single time and only the third one falls short, which is the one thing stopping this slot from ever moving; this makes it two sets, the same fix you accepted on the rope pushdown.

You asked on 28 August why Pull A calls for three face pull sets when you think two is right, and you did two that night — Pull B already runs two, so this makes the two days agree with each other and with you.
